report: AWS and GCP necessity audit - the nine-disagreement audit of right-tool-for-the-job.html
method: Both script blocks of the audited page were executed in a Node vm against its own scenario library; for each scenario the pattern named by its written advice was compared with the pattern its deterministic engine ranks first.

discountedHypotheses.hypothesis: A burst-heavy scenario modelled at zero because a daily free allowance had been double-counted.
discountedHypotheses.outcome: Not reproduced. Five million requests and 25 million CPU milliseconds sit inside the Workers Paid included allowance of ten million requests, so the modelled zero is correct, and the audit records the check rather than the hypothesis.

integrity: No file in the audited artifact was modified. Each item below carries a proposed correction for a separate, deliberate change.

findings.title: A static-publication pattern has no storage member
findings.detail: The gh-pages-static pattern declares a delivery member and a build member and no member with the storage role. Its static-site template sets storageKind to objects, so the storage gate eliminates it with "nowhere to keep data at rest". Reproduced headlessly.
findings.impact: Two of the nine disagreements (sc-03 and sc-30) follow from this one defect, and the pattern would otherwise have ranked first on relevance in both.
findings.proposed: Add a storage member representing the repository as the object store, or exempt a delivery-only pattern when the declared dataset fits the published-site limit. Not applied here: changing another artifact is a separate, deliberate change.

findings.title: A gate message interpolates an undefined capability
findings.detail: The same rejection renders as "GH Pages static offers only  consistency for authoritative reads" — two spaces where a value should be. The check reads a capability the pattern members do not define and formats an empty string.
findings.impact: Cosmetically trivial, but it is the visible symptom of an incomplete capability record, which is the same root cause as the finding above.
findings.proposed: Where a capability value is absent, report the gate as not applicable, or fail with an explicit "capability not recorded" reason.

findings.title: Incumbent credit is granted to a provider label, not a platform
findings.detail: Relevance awards a bonus when existingInfra matches the pattern provider, so a hybrid pattern collects the Cloudflare bonus it did not earn, and a self-hosted operator gets credit only for patterns whose provider label is conventional.
findings.impact: Contributes to sc-06, sc-29 and sc-33: the local-first and Cloudflare-first answers lose a tie they should win.
findings.proposed: Attribute incumbent credit per platform owned, not per provider label on a topology.

findings.title: A capability label can outrank a requirement mismatch
findings.detail: Relevance is dominated by the pattern fits list, so a pattern whose defining requirement a scenario override has removed still scores as an exact fit, and a materially suitable pattern whose fits list omits a label scores zero and sorts last.
findings.impact: Responsible for sc-20 and sc-32, and a contributing cause in sc-22.
findings.proposed: Score against requirement values and their consequences rather than workload-type names, and give a pattern with no label match a floor relevance when its members satisfy every stated requirement.

items.cause: The gh-pages-static pattern has no member with the storage role while its static-site template declares storageKind objects, so the storage gate eliminates the pattern before relevance is consulted.
evidence: Rejection: "GH Pages static has nowhere to keep data at rest, and this workload needs objects persistence."
The same rejection fails the consistency gate and renders as "offers only  consistency..." with an empty value where a capability should be.
On relevance the eliminated pattern would have scored 5 (static-site + pub:git + github) against the winner's 3. It was the intended answer.
items.verdictReason: Written advice is right and the engine never had a chance to agree: a defect, not the reasoning, produced the disagreement.
items.reuse: This page treats a missing capability field as a validation failure to surface, never as a silent rejection, and models repository-backed static hosting as storage that exists.
items.proposed: Add a storage member to the static-publication pattern, or exempt a delivery-only pattern from the storage gate when its dataset fits the published-site limit.

items.cause: Identical to sc-03: same pattern, same missing role, same gate. The scenarios differ only in transfer volume and frequency.
evidence: The same two violations reproduce with the same message text.
The written advice adds a consideration the engine has no field for: the only defensible reason to move is a custom domain on a zone already paid for.
items.verdictReason: Written advice supported. Two scenarios, one defect, which means the disagreement count overstates the number of distinct problems by one.
items.reuse: Two scenarios sharing one cause are reported here as one finding with a scenario count, not as two findings.
items.proposed: The same correction as sc-03; nothing separately actionable.

items.cause: Both patterns reach relevance 4 and the tie breaks on operational suitability: 4.38 for the larger runner against 4.05 for the local pattern. The self-hosted incumbent gets no relevance credit, because the bonus applies only when a pattern's provider label is conventional and the local-first hybrid is labelled hybrid.
evidence: existingInfra self-hosted with provider hybrid produced no bonus; the same value with provider conventional would have.
The winner models at $21.95/month against $2.24 for the pattern the written advice prefers.
Cost is consulted only after relevance and suitability, so the dearer answer was never compared on price.
items.verdictReason: Written advice supported. The engine pays for the must-be-awake caveat twice and never credits what the advice values: the hardware is already paid for and already idle.
items.reuse: This page grants incumbent credit per owned platform rather than per provider label, and lets cost reach the ranking whenever two options sit inside a stated suitability band.
items.proposed: Extend the incumbent bonus to any pattern containing a member the operator already owns, and print the cost delta beside a tie-break.

items.cause: The template sets 256 MB of memory and 1 GB of scratch on the upload path, which eliminates the Workers and Queues members at 128 MB and no disk. The written design deliberately keeps bytes out of the Worker, so those figures describe an implementation the recommended architecture does not use.
evidence: Four violations, two per member: 128 MB against 256 MB, and no scratch space against 1 GB.
The written advice names the mechanism: a presigned upload to R2 removes the Worker from the byte path entirely.
items.verdictReason: Both supported under their own assumptions. The engine answered the requirement it was given correctly; the requirement, not the engine, turns an implementation choice into a constraint.
items.reuse: This page separates a workload's intrinsic resource envelope from the envelope of a chosen implementation, and only the intrinsic envelope may eliminate a platform. Derived figures become cautions.
items.proposed: Mark template-derived resource figures as derived, and downgrade them to cautions when a scenario's own design avoids them.

items.cause: The scenario sets the OS to linux, removes the native binary requirement and reduces concurrency to one, deleting the cross-platform requirement — yet the CI matrix keeps an exact-name relevance of 4 against 3 for a scheduled batch, with suitability running the other way.
evidence: Relevance 4 against 3, suitability 3.69 against 3.98: the engine picks the option it has just ranked as worse to operate.
The matrix pattern's defining property — many operating systems — is no longer required by anything in the requirement set, and nothing in the model can observe that.
items.verdictReason: Written advice supported. The engine over-credits a label match by more than the suitability difference it then ignores.
items.reuse: This page scores candidates against requirement values and their consequences, never against a workload-type name.
items.proposed: Weight pattern relevance by which requirements remain after scenario overrides.

items.cause: The queue pattern's member set already contains the request-serving Worker and the queue that the webhook pattern denotes; the webhook pattern adds a durable workflow for multi-step follow-up. Both survive, both score relevance 3, and the engine prefers the simpler and cheaper of the two because a durable retry requirement is recorded as a caution rather than a gate.
evidence: Both patterns remain feasible; the difference is $3.75 against $4.55 a month.
The written advice describes a superset: acknowledge in milliseconds, enqueue the work, and let a workflow handle what must survive retries.
items.verdictReason: Both supported, because they denote nearly the same topology. Neither is wrong; the model has two overlapping patterns and cannot express a queue plus durable workflow as one answer.
items.reuse: This page defines patterns as composable roles with an explicit superset relation, and reports a disagreement as an equivalent topology rather than a conflict when one pattern's roles contain the other's.
items.proposed: Record an explicit superset relation between overlapping patterns and prefer the specific one when the requirement names the extra capability.

items.cause: Relevance awards a bonus when the existing infrastructure matches a pattern's provider, and the rule accepts a hybrid provider as a match, so the GitHub-plus-R2 pattern collects the Cloudflare incumbent bonus it did not earn and reaches relevance 5 against 4 for the pure Cloudflare pattern.
evidence: The scenario sets the trigger to event; R2 event notifications are consumed by a Cloudflare Worker, and the hybrid pattern orchestrates from GitHub, which no gate notices.
Both options model at zero on this requirement set, so relevance alone decided it.
items.verdictReason: Written advice supported. The incumbent credit is mis-awarded and the trigger semantics of the scenario are ignored, which is the more serious of the two.
items.reuse: This page attributes incumbent credit per platform owned rather than per provider label, and treats who can receive a given trigger as a hard gate for event-driven work.
items.proposed: Remove hybrid from the incumbent-bonus provider test, or replace the test with a per-platform ownership check.

items.cause: The queue pattern's fits list omits the read-only API workload type, so on this requirement set it scores relevance 0 and sorts below everything that matches the label, despite the highest operational suitability in the set and a cost below the winner's.
evidence: Relevance 0 against 3 for the winner, with suitability 4.53 against 4.55 and cost $3.60 against $0.

A suspicion that the $0 was a free-tier error did not survive reproduction: 5 million requests and 25 million CPU milliseconds sit inside the Workers Paid included allowance of 10 million requests, so the modelled zero is correct. The audit records the check rather than the hypothesis.
items.verdictReason: Written advice supported. A materially suitable pattern is invisible because of a label list: a data deficiency rather than a scoring bug.
items.reuse: This page derives relevance from the capabilities a candidate actually has, and every free allowance in its catalogue carries its period so a monthly model cannot spend a daily allowance.
items.proposed: Add api-backend and public-web to the queue pattern's fits list, or replace the label list with a capability-derived fit score.

items.cause: The written advice is explicitly conditional — a daemon with a queue and a filesystem belongs on a container host, a bounded job belongs on a scale-to-zero container — and the requirement set has no field distinguishing a bounded job from a long-lived service, so the engine cannot see the fork it is being asked about.
evidence: The engine returns the local pattern at relevance 4 and $6.14 ahead of the container pattern at relevance 3 and $35: legitimate for the bounded branch and $29 a month cheaper.
Nothing in the requirement vocabulary separates a daemon from a job, which is the entire content of the written recommendation.
items.verdictReason: Engine supported for the bounded case; the written advice is a conditional the model cannot express. Neither is an error — the requirement vocabulary is incomplete.
items.reuse: This page asks bounded-or-long-lived as an explicit input, models long-lived services with their own always-on floor, and never presents a conditional recommendation as a single verdict.
items.proposed: Add a lifetime field to the requirement schema and gate always-on patterns on it.
